prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t truthfully name one single “best” lawyer for every truck accident — that depends on the specifics of your case and what you value (trial experience, record of big verdicts, client communication, cost, etc.). I can, however, quickly help you find very strong candidates and tell you exactly how to evaluate them and what to do now.

Immediate steps (do these now)
- Get medical care and keep all records.  
- Call police and get a copy of the crash report.  
- Preserve evidence: photos, video, witness names, truck number, license plate, company name.  
- Don’t give recorded statements to insurers until you’ve talked to an attorney.  
- Be aware of the Texas statute of limitations: generally 2 years from the crash date for personal injury (shorter in some circumstances).

How to find the right Dallas truck-accident lawyer
- Look for attorneys/firms that specifically handle commercial trucking collisions (not just “car” or general PI). Trucking cases use different rules (FMCSA regs, logbooks, ELD data, maintenance records, driver hiring/discipline files).  
- Pick a lawyer with experience litigating and taking trucking cases to trial — trucking companies and insurers often only take large claims seriously when the lawyer will actually try the case.  
- Check reputation: verdicts/settlements, peer ratings (Martindale-Hubbell), Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Avvo, and client reviews.  
- Confirm they have resources to investigate (accident reconstructionists, trucking experts, medical experts). Truck cases are document- and expert-heavy.  
- Ask about contingency fee structure and who pays upfront costs (most work on contingency; costs are typically advanced and reimbursed from recovery).

Key questions to ask when you interview an attorney
1. How many truck/CMV cases have you handled? How many in Dallas County?  
2. What percentage of your practice is trucking collisions?  
3. Have you taken a trucking case to trial? Can you give examples of verdicts/settlements?  
4. Who will handle my case day-to-day (partner vs. associate)?  
5. How do you charge (contingency %) and what costs will be advanced?  
6. How will you investigate the trucking company (ELD/logs, maintenance, driver record)?  
7. What is a realistic value/range for my case and timeline?  
8. Can you provide references from former clients?

Typical contingency-fee expectations (general guidance)
- Common ranges: ~33% if settled before suit; higher if filed or tried (often 33–40% or on a sliding scale). Confirm exact terms in writing.

Resources for locating top lawyers in Dallas
- Texas State Bar Lawyer Referral Service  
- Super Lawyers (Texas/Dallas lists)  
- Martindale-Hubbell peer ratings  
- Avvo and Google/Yelp reviews  
- Local trial lawyer associations (Texas Trial Lawyers Association)

If you want, I can:
- Search and give a short vetted list (3–5) of Dallas lawyers/firms with strong truck-accident records (I’ll include links, recent verdicts/settlements, and contact tips). If you want that, tell me any preferences (e.g., maximum distance from you in Dallas, whether you prefer a large firm or a solo/small firm, how severe the injuries are).

Would you like me to compile a targeted shortlist now? If so, tell me where in Dallas the crash happened and any key facts (injury severity, whether commercial truck clearly at fault, police report done).
